claims.title: Indigenous settlement
claims.summary: Arawak, Carib, and other Indigenous peoples occupy the coast and interior of present-day Suriname over many centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Suriname: From the Arawak and Carib coast to a Dutch plantation colony built on sugar and slavery, the Maroon republics of the forest, the most ethnically plural society in the Americas, and an independent nation born in 1975.", terralore.co/country/SUR/chronicle#ev-3000bce-indigenous-settlement, claim TL:SUR:event:3000bce:indigenous-settlement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: European voyages sight the coast
claims.summary: Columbus sights the Guiana coast in 1498 and Spanish expeditions sail along it soon after, but no lasting settlement follows.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Suriname: From the Arawak and Carib coast to a Dutch plantation colony built on sugar and slavery, the Maroon republics of the forest, the most ethnically plural society in the Americas, and an independent nation born in 1975.", terralore.co/country/SUR/chronicle#ev-1498-european-voyages-sight-the-coast, claim TL:SUR:event:1498:european-voyages-sight-the-coast, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: English settlement under Willoughby
claims.summary: Lord Francis Willoughby of Barbados plants an English sugar colony on the Suriname River, with the first enslaved Africans set to work.

sources.label: Francis Willoughby, 5th Baron Willoughby of Parham

claims.title: Dutch capture of the colony
claims.summary: A Dutch force from Zeeland seizes the English colony during the Second Anglo-Dutch War.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Suriname: From the Arawak and Carib coast to a Dutch plantation colony built on sugar and slavery, the Maroon republics of the forest, the most ethnically plural society in the Americas, and an independent nation born in 1975.", terralore.co/country/SUR/chronicle#ev-1667-dutch-capture-of-the-colony, claim TL:SUR:event:1667:dutch-capture-of-the-colony, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Treaty of Breda
claims.summary: The peace confirms Suriname to the Dutch while England keeps New Netherland and New Amsterdam, the future New York.

sources.label: Treaty of Breda, 1667
sources.publisher: Historical Society of the New York Courts

claims.title: The sugar-slavery economy
claims.summary: Dutch Suriname becomes a plantation colony worked by enslaved Africans under exceptionally harsh conditions, with Paramaribo as its capital and port.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Suriname: From the Arawak and Carib coast to a Dutch plantation colony built on sugar and slavery, the Maroon republics of the forest, the most ethnically plural society in the Americas, and an independent nation born in 1975.", terralore.co/country/SUR/chronicle#ev-1667-the-sugar-slavery-economy, claim TL:SUR:event:1667:the-sugar-slavery-economy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Maroon peace treaties
claims.summary: Unable to defeat the Maroons, the Dutch sign treaties from the 1760s recognising the freedom of the Ndyuka, Saramaka, and Matawai and their lands in the interior.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Suriname: From the Arawak and Carib coast to a Dutch plantation colony built on sugar and slavery, the Maroon republics of the forest, the most ethnically plural society in the Americas, and an independent nation born in 1975.", terralore.co/country/SUR/chronicle#ev-1760-maroon-peace-treaties, claim TL:SUR:event:1760:maroon-peace-treaties, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of the Maroon leader Boni
claims.summary: Boni, leader of the Aluku, is killed after years of guerrilla war against colonial forces, becoming an enduring symbol of resistance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Suriname: From the Arawak and Carib coast to a Dutch plantation colony built on sugar and slavery, the Maroon republics of the forest, the most ethnically plural society in the Americas, and an independent nation born in 1975.", terralore.co/country/SUR/chronicle#ev-1793-death-of-the-maroon-leader-boni, claim TL:SUR:event:1793:death-of-the-maroon-leader-boni, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Abolition of slavery
claims.summary: The Netherlands abolishes slavery in Suriname, though the freed are bound to a further decade of supervised apprenticeship until 1873.

sources.label: Suriname death records reveal fate of Hindustani indentured labourers after slavery

claims.title: Hindustani indentured labour
claims.summary: Contract labourers from British India, the Hindustanis, are recruited to the plantations; roughly thirty-four thousand arrive over the period.

sources.label: Suriname death records reveal fate of Hindustani indentured labourers after slavery

claims.title: Javanese indentured labour
claims.summary: Indentured workers from Java join the plantation workforce, numbering some thirty-three thousand and forming a community unique in the Caribbean.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Suriname: From the Arawak and Carib coast to a Dutch plantation colony built on sugar and slavery, the Maroon republics of the forest, the most ethnically plural society in the Americas, and an independent nation born in 1975.", terralore.co/country/SUR/chronicle#ev-1890-javanese-indentured-labour, claim TL:SUR:event:1890:javanese-indentured-labour, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence from the Netherlands
claims.summary: Suriname becomes a sovereign state; Johan Ferrier is the first president and the United States recognises the nation the same day.

sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.title: Military coup
claims.summary: Non-commissioned officers overthrow the elected government; Desi Bouterse emerges as the regime's strongman, ruling by decree.

claims.title: The December murders
claims.summary: Fifteen leading opponents of military rule are seized and killed at Fort Zeelandia in Paramaribo, drawing international condemnation.

claims.title: The Interior War
claims.summary: The mainly Maroon Jungle Commando under Ronnie Brunswijk fights the army in the east until a ceasefire in 1989 and a peace accord in 1992.
